chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from 'Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding al-Mut'ah, he said: 'It is not one of the four, because it is not divorced, nor does it entail inheritance, and it is merely a hired [contract].' And he said: 'Its waiting period is five and forty nights.'
As for what was narrated - al-Saffar from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from 'Abdullah ibn Muskan, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding al-Mut'ah, he said: 'It is one of the four.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal status and waiting period of Mut'ah marriage in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential debate regarding the nature of *al-Mut'ah* (temporary marriage), contrasting the view that it is a distinct contractual category lacking divorce and inheritance rights with the position affirming it as one of the four primary marriage types. The specific mention of a forty-five-night waiting period (*iddah*) underscores the unique temporal boundaries that distinguish it from permanent unions in Shia fiqh.
